title: A congressional representative just proposed killing America’s border tower program
gist: Rep. Delia Ramirez (D-IL) plans the Reimagining Safety Act to terminate the roughly billion-dollar US southern border surveillance tower program, citing MIT Technology Review findings that nearly one in four analyzed border deaths (about 1,100 people, 2015-2026) occurred within tower range. The bill is part of a broader plan to dismantle DHS and faces a steep uphill battle in Congress.

insights.claim: An MIT Technology Review investigation found nearly one in four border deaths it analyzed between 2015 and early 2026 occurred within the advertised range of US southern border surveillance towers.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: Documented performance gaps create political and contract-renewal risk for border-surveillance technology vendors.
insights.locator: The announcement comes just days after publication

insights.claim: The Department of Homeland Security does not track deaths near border surveillance towers or other metrics on the towers' success or failure.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: Absence of outcome metrics weakens the government's ability to defend the program's budget against cuts.

insights.claim: Rep. Delia Ramirez cited reporting that nearly 1,100 people died within range of the billion-dollar border surveillance tower system between 2015 and 2026, declaring that the towers do not work.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: Investigative journalism is directly feeding legislative attacks on surveillance procurement programs.
insights.quote: The towers that we have paid a billion dollars to just don’t work.
insights.locator: Ramirez, who sits on the Homeland Security Committee

themes.theme: Reimagining Safety Act and DHS dismantling

insights.claim: Rep. Delia Ramirez's Reimagining Safety Act would terminate the southern border surveillance tower program as part of a broader plan to replace DHS with a new Department of Community Safety and move CISA, FEMA, TSA, and customs functions to other federal agencies.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: Signals the direction of progressive Democratic policy on homeland security spending; bill text due in the next few weeks.
insights.locator: The legislation is intended to be part of a broader proposal

insights.claim: Proposals to dismantle DHS have been introduced before without getting far, and this one faces a steep uphill battle since even some Democrats prefer reforming rather than dismantling the department.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: Near-term passage odds are low; treat the bill as a signal of political risk rather than an imminent budget change.
insights.locator: It will not be the first time that a bill to dismantle

insights.claim: Ramirez has institutional leverage as a member of the House committee overseeing DHS and as ranking member of the Homeland Security Committee's cybersecurity subcommittee.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: Oversight roles let her pressure DHS surveillance programs via hearings even if the bill stalls.

insights.claim: Ramirez frames the legislation as limiting state surveillance, curbing unlawful data abuses and militarized enforcement, and beginning a separate civil immigration system.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: Data-driven immigration surveillance and enforcement tech is a named political target, a headline risk for govtech and surveillance vendors.
insights.quote: We're limiting state surveillance, we're reigning unlawful abuses of data and curbing the militarized enforcement.

insights.claim: Public support for abolishing ICE has grown following the second Trump administration's visible enforcement operations in US cities, expansion of detention capacity, and shootings by ICE and CBP agents.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: Shifting public sentiment raises long-term political risk for detention and enforcement contractors.

insights.so_what: Organized advocacy targeting ICE's technology stack is translating into legislation.

insights.claim: Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin flatly rejected calls to abolish DHS, saying it will never happen.
insights.speaker: Eileen Guo
insights.so_what: The administration is firmly opposed, reinforcing that the program is safe under current leadership.
insights.quote: Radical leftists are calling to defund the police and abolish DHS. It’s NEVER going to happen.
